The company rolled out Microsoft 365 to reduce the number of internal apps and better connect systems for easier collaboration. This helped make employees more efficient and reduced routine tasks.

Sensei cut its third-party tools from 15 to 6, saving more than $60,000 annually. This not only improved data security and made it easier to automate workflows, but it also freed up employees to focus on the strategic work they were hired to do.

With roughly 160 employees around the globe and a lean IT department, Sensei wanted to automate and streamline. Logging into 15 IT solutions was cumbersome, and it was difficult to connect data and keep it updated across systems. Storing information in multiple tools posed security and data management concerns.

DeMarco says, “Microsoft 365 helps us scale with finite staff and budget while protecting customers’ data and our IT environment. The integration enables us to get more value from existing solutions, and Microsoft apps are the language that employees speak.”
